text:
Maria Lopez: ran an nsys capture on dev-box-3 for the KV cache flush path when batching large seqs — looks like PCIe/NVLink transfers are dominating at scale. trace: https://redwood-internal/trace/1748001234/nvtrace
Jeff Wong: can you paste the nsys command you used? want to repro locally
Maria Lopez: sure, ran: ```nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt,nvtx --output=kv-1748 ./run_inference --model swish-v2 --batch 8 --seq 1024``` captured ~120s
Samir Patel: quick summary from the timeline: ~42% of visible time in memcpy H2D/D2H, lots of serialized peer copies (cuMemcpyPeerAsync) and frequent stalls where pageable memory forced syncs. nvshow shows many "cudaMemcpy" events with size ~40MB repeated.
Kai Nguyen: interesting — did we switch to pageable allocations for the KV cache in the kernel-selection change last week? I recall a patch to relax host mem pressure that defaulted to cudaMallocHost(false) fallback.
Maria Lopez: yes, commit e3f4a6a changed allocation path to avoid blocking on host alloc, ended up using normal host malloc for some flows. I think that's exposing pageable -> pinned fallback behavior and incurring implicit staging copies.
Jeff Wong: pageable -> pinned staging will cause extra memcpy H2D on the driver side and can also block streams. Could explain the stalls.
Samir Patel: nsys summary snippet (from report): ```
CUDA API: cudaMemcpy* total time: 51.2s (42.6%)
Kernel time (compute): 31.0s (25.8%)
CPU idle waiting on ioctl: lots of wait events during memcpy
```
Maria Lopez: also saw many cuMemcpyPeerAsync events across GPUs tied to NVLink domains, but their overlap was poor — they were largely serialized due to our batching loop doing synchronous stage per micro-batch.
Kai Nguyen: two quick experiments to isolate:
1) Force KV alloc with pinned memory via `cudaHostAlloc` or `cuMemHostRegister` and rerun nsys.
2) Keep pageable but run `cudaMemPrefetchAsync` to device early (if using managed) or pre-copy in parallel stream to overlap.
Jeff Wong: also test enabling P2P (cuDeviceEnablePeerAccess) + using cuMemcpyPeerAsync between devices; NVLink will help only when topology supports it.
Samir Patel: I ran a short A/B earlier: pinned pool reduced end-to-end memcpy time by ~60% and removed many stall events. But pinned approach increased host memory pressure and OOM risk under high concurrency.
Maria Lopez: log snippet from the capture showing stall and fallback:
```
[CUDA memcpy H2D] size=41943040 start=12.345s end=12.456s pinned_fallback=yes
[cuMemcpyPeerAsync] srcGpu=0 dstGpu=1 start=12.460s end=12.490s overlap=0
```
Jeff Wong: actionable: revert the allocation fallback in kernel-selection branch for a canary build and run perf tests with pinned pool + prefetch + p2p enabled.
Kai Nguyen: I'll run the pinned vs pageable matrix on dev-box-3 (same hw as prod) and upload traces to the same folder. Will also try batching heuristic tweak: increase inner micro-batch aggregation so we do fewer large H2D bursts but bigger aggregated memcpy (better throughput, maybe worse latency).
Maria Lopez: another angle: our kernel selector in v2.3.1 switched to fused attention kernels which reduce compute but increase KV cache churn. That could increase transfer volume per step and make transfers the new bottleneck.
Samir Patel: reproduced that: toggling kernel variant back to unfused reduced transfer volume substantially (less frequent KV reshaping). So both kernel selection and allocation choice matter.
Jeff Wong: propose test plan (short):
- baseline (current): fused kernels + pageable pool (capture)
- pinned pool + fused kernels
- pageable + fused kernels + prefetch async
- unfused kernels + pageable
capture nsys and perfetto for each, compare memcpy time and overlap metrics
Kai Nguyen: assign: Kai=run matrix, Maria=collect config + commit hashes, Samir=analyze traces and prepare perf diff, Jeff=hold canary rollback ready if perf confirms regressed path
Maria Lopez: uploaded the first trace here: https://redwood-internal/trace/1748001234/kv-1748.nsys-rep
sre-bot: scheduled job #582: nsys-analysis (kv-hotspots) queued on dev-box-3
deploy-bot: note: if we revert kernel-selection in canary, remember to bump canary image tag for Dedicated clusters :warning:
Jeff Wong: thanks — let's sync tomorrow after traces. :thumbsup:
